chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all of them, from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the divorce of the young boy who has not yet reached puberty, and his dowry. He said: 'If he divorces [her] according to the Sunnah and places the dowry in its proper place and right, then there is no harm, and it is valid.'

key_terms.طَلاَقِ الْغُلاَمِ: Divorce of the young boy/pre-pubescent male
key_terms.وَلَمْ يَحْتَلِمْ: And he has not yet reached puberty (ejaculated)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the divorce of a pre-pubescent boy in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies that a pre-pubescent boy's divorce is valid according to the Sunnah, provided his dowry is properly allocated, reflecting the Shia view that financial obligations apply even before full maturity. It highlights the role of the guardian in executing these rites, ensuring the legal and financial integrity of the marriage contract is maintained despite the boy's lack of full legal capacity.
